title: Nonhelema
summary: Nonhelema, sister of Shawnee leader Cornstalk, was a Chalakatha chief, diplomat, and warrior who held influence at Lower Shawneetown on the Ohio River.
bodyMarkdown:
Nonhelema Hokolesqua (active mid-1700s–1786), sister of the Shawnee leader Cornstalk, was a Chalakatha (Chillicothe) chief, diplomat, and warrior whom settlers nicknamed “the Grenadier” for her height. By mid-century she held influence at Lower Shawneetown in Greenup County and later warned American posts of British-allied raids even after Cornstalk’s 1777 murder at Fort Randolph.

In 1785 Congress answered her land petition with a ration pension instead of Ohio acreage. In 1786 Kentucky militia under Benjamin Logan struck her Ohio village; her husband Moluntha was killed (by Hugh McGary in the usual accounts), and she died later that year after captivity.
